title: The burning tail
hookLine: caught and set on fire to shame him, Hanuman burns Lanka; the fire comes home to the one who lit it
carry: karma: the fire you light comes home

cards: The job is done. He's found Sita and has her jewel. He could slip away tonight and no one in Lanka would know.
Instead, Hanuman wants to see the enemy up close, so he does something loud. He tears up the royal garden, tree by tree, and fights off wave after wave of warriors.
Finally Ravana's son, Indrajit, binds him with a divine weapon. Hanuman could break free. He lets himself be dragged into the court of the ten-headed king.
He wanted to be caught: it was the only way in the front door.

teach.b: Before Ravana, Hanuman speaks plainly: give Sita back, make peace with Rama. Ravana, furious, orders him killed. His younger brother, Vibhishana, objects: you don't kill a messenger; that's not how kings behave.
Remember Vibhishana; he matters later. So Ravana picks a humiliation instead. A monkey's pride is his tail, he says.
The guards wrap the tail in rags, soak it in oil, set it alight, and parade Hanuman through the streets to laughter. Then he shrinks, slips his ropes, grows huge again and leaps onto the rooftops.
Tail blazing, he jumps from palace to palace, and the golden city goes up in flames.

teach.h: SITA PRAYS: BE COOL FOR HIM.
teach.b: When Sita hears they've set his tail on fire, she prays to Agni, god of fire, that it be cool for him. Mid-leap, Hanuman notices it isn't hurting him at all. Then panic: what if I've burned the garden where she is?
Now notice who lit the fire. Ravana chose it, to shame a messenger. By nightfall it was his own city burning.
Many teachers read this as karma, your seventh word: every action bears fruit, and the fruit comes back to the one who acted.

No one had to punish Ravana; his own act ripened on his own roofs, and the woman he wronged, praying, was the one place it couldn't touch. So the lesson isn't burn things down. It's in Ravana's hands.

teach.h: KARMA: THE FIRE YOU LIGHT COMES HOME.
teach.b: The fire you light comes home.

how: The burning of Lanka is a favorite scene in Ramlila performances across North India, and devotees recite it as part of the Sundara Kanda.

o: the ocean Hanuman leaps across to reach the demon king
the forest kingdom where Sugriva hides from his brother

Hanuman is caught because he's too tired to fight
he lets himself be taken, to get into Ravana's court.
Ravana's brother argues against killing Hanuman

games.q: you're Ravana. a captured messenger stands in your court and tells you to give Sita back. what do you do?
o: shame him: set his tail on fire.
have him killed on the spot.
games.why: Vibhishana stops the killing, so Ravana chooses to shame him with fire. by nightfall that fire is burning Ravana's own city. karma.

practice: Sit and breathe. Bring to mind something said or done to shame you, and notice the pull to throw it back. Don't.

Picture handing that fire over, the way Sita prayed to Agni, and asking that it burn no one, including you. If you pray, say it to God in your own words. If you don't, breathe out slowly, and set it down.

wordCard.voice: Lanka. Ravana's golden island city, set ablaze by the tail they lit to shame Hanuman.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the island city of Ravana in the Ramayana.

carryVoice: Your line: karma: the fire you light comes home. Ravana learned it in his own city. That's day thirty-four.
